fixes.explanation: David asks the LORD to “show no mercy to the wicked traitors.” (Psalm 59:5). That's a heavy line, and I think it comes from a man who is scared and hurting. And it's right there in the verse, plain as flour on an apron.

The city is the word. David says his enemies return in the evening, “…snarling like dogs and prowling around the city.” (Psalm 59:6). Dogs on the loose in the middle of town is a scary picture, and that's the picture David paints. Verse 14 says it again.

Their own words give them away: “For who can hear us?” (Psalm 59:7). They talk like nobody is listening. But one verse later, David says of the LORD, “But You, O LORD, laugh at them…” (Psalm 59:8). It's like trash-talking your boss in the break room while the boss stands right behind you.

Giving up never comes up in what the enemies say. The only words David quotes from them are “For who can hear us?” (Psalm 59:7). That's the sound of people talking like it's private. Sharp words, and a whole lot of confidence that nobody is listening.
That's what David says: “God will let me stare down my foes.” (Psalm 59:10). It comes right after “My God of loving devotion will come to meet me…” So David is counting on God to come to him.

This one is true. David says, “My God of loving devotion will come to meet me; God will let me stare down my foes.” (Psalm 59:10). He talks like he's counting on it. And the verse says it's God who comes to meet him.

David gives his reason right in the verse: “Do not kill them, or my people will forget.” (Psalm 59:11). He doesn't want his people to forget. Then he asks God to “Scatter them by Your power…” instead. It's a strange prayer at first, but the reason is right there in the verse.

Nothing in the verse talks about the enemies turning back. David's reason is “Do not kill them, or my people will forget.” (Psalm 59:11). What's on his mind is his people and their forgetting, not what happens to the enemies. Then he asks God to “Scatter them by Your power…”

David asks, “…let them be trapped in their pride, in the curses and lies they utter.” (Psalm 59:12). Right before that, he mentions the sins of their mouths and the words of their lips. It lines up with the sharp words from verse 7. Pride and lies are the ones he names.

David says, “But I will sing of Your strength and proclaim Your loving devotion in the morning.” (Psalm 59:16). The enemies return in the evening, and David says he will sing in the morning. He sets a song right next to all that snarling. I think that's something to keep in your pocket.

David says it the other way around. He calls God “…my fortress, my refuge in times of trouble.” (Psalm 59:16). Times of trouble are exactly when he's leaning on God. The heading mentions Saul sending men to watch David's house in order to kill him, so trouble is in the picture.
